english.title: Fly relevant UK helicopter with max take-off mass 5,700kg or less without at least two pilots
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the

(A)_[operator]_
(B)_[pilot in command]_

of a helicopter registered in the United Kingdom, namely **(..SPECIFY HELICOPTER..), which did not carry at least two pilots as members of its flight crew when it was flying for the purpose of public transport, had a maximum take-off mass of 5,700kg or less and
(C)_[was flying in circumstances where the pilot in command was required to comply with the Instrument Flight Rules]_
(D)_[was flying at night on a special VFR flight]_
english.legislation: Contrary to articles 110(1) and 265(6) of the Air Navigation Order 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
were the operator or pilot in command of a helicopter registered in the United Kingdom
which did not carry at least two pilots as members of its flight crew
when it was flying for the purpose of public transport, had a maximum take-off mass of 5,700kg or less and was flying in circumstances where the pilot in command was required to comply with the Instrument Flight Rules OR

english.notes:
A helicopter described in the wording is not required to carry two pilots if
(a) it is equipped with an autopilot with altitude hold and heading mode which is serviceable on take-off;
(b) it is equipped with such an autopilot even though before take-off the autopilot is found to be un-serviceable, if the helicopter flies in accordance with arrangements approved by the CAA; or
(c) it is flying by day and remains clear of cloud and with the surface in sight.
